name: Bajaj Consumer Care Ltd
title: Bajaj Consumer Care Ltd - 533229 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consumer hair-oil FMCG with no capacity signal; H1 revenue up 28% to INR674 crore and gross margin fell to 59.9% in Q2, cushioned by cost cuts, with a ~5% price increase planned for Q3.

triggers.label: Another ~5% consumer price increase in Q3
triggers.quote: we will now follow it up with another round of price increase and ml-age reduction in quarter 3. In this round, we are approximately taking a 5% increase in consumer price

triggers.label: Gross margin 59.9% in Q2
triggers.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter were at 59.9%, and overall for the first half of the year at 60.8%.

triggers.label: ADHO unit volume up double digit
triggers.quote: has delivered double -digit unit volume growth

triggers.label: FY27 high-teens growth expected
triggers.quote: for the year, we are expecting a high teens, and that's what we've just said

guidance.quote: for the year, we are expecting a high teens, and that's what we've just said
Over the long term, we want to aspire for a double-digit growth
expanding direct distribution by 10%, and we want to take this objective as a year-on-year objective

red_flags.label: Gross margin down sequentially on input costs
red_flags.quote: Despite the sequential reduction in gross margin, our teams have been able to rally around and deliver very strong savings in fixed costs

red_flags.label: Shift to third-party manufacturing; stock-in-trade purchases up
red_flags.quote: we have outsourced basically the production of one of our factories in Guwahati from a company-owned facility to a third-party-run facility

summary.headline: Bajaj Consumer Care Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.7% to INR233 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% and H1 revenue up 28% to INR674 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 revenue of INR233 crore (+2.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR53 crore (25% margin) and PAT of INR70 crore (21% margin), with H1 revenue of INR674 crore (+28%) and H1 PAT of INR141 crore (+75%). Gross margin fell sequentially to 59.9% in Q2 (60.8% for H1) due to raw material inflation from the West Asia war and edible oil prices, offset by fixed and employee cost savings. Almond Drops posted double-digit unit volume growth, and management guided to a high-teens growth for the year and a further ~5% consumer price increase in Q3. Aarohan 2.0 was announced as a pan-India direct distribution expansion programme targeting 10% expansion per year.

financial_highlights.change: Sequential reduction in Q2 (no YoY figure stated)

segments.name: Almond Drops Hair Oil (ADHO)
segments.commentary: Delivered double-digit unit volume growth in Q2, led by small and medium packs; price-point packs are in the teens % of value and organized trade is close to 30% of company value sales. Management said the brand is being reinvigorated with a new 'hair strength leading to beauty' TV campaign and 360-degree support.

segments.name: Coconut franchise
segments.commentary: Management said it saw strong volume growth across channels; no free-volume or grammage addition was stated, and pricing was negative.

segments.name: Growth portfolio (amla, body lotion, Banjara's)
segments.commentary: Profitability substantially improved; amla oil mix being tested in general trade, body lotion upgraded and to be tested on e-commerce, and Banjara's extended into adjacent categories (lip balm, colour shampoo) with pilots in the four southern states.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Grew ahead of company growth for H1 and showed a sharp profitability improvement; Bangladesh grew in the teens amid a tough operating environment.

guidance_outlook: Management expects high-teens revenue growth for FY27 and reiterated long-term aspiration of double-digit growth; no quarterly guidance given.
A further price increase of ~5% in consumer price terms in Q3 FY27, split roughly equally between 2-3% frontal price increase and an equivalent ml-age reduction.
Priority is protecting and growing absolute EBITDA pool rather than EBITDA margin percentage; non-working A&P to be tightly managed until cost pressures ease.
Gross margin outlook not given; management said cost environment remains volatile and raw material buying is kept lean.
Aarohan 2.0: pan-India programme targeting 10% expansion of direct distribution each year, with urban reach up 10% and rural higher over the next six quarters.
No M&A deal currently in progress, per management.
capex_capacity: Project Aarohan phases 1-3 (13 states, 8 quarters) nearly complete: over 1 lakh outlets added, 1,000+ distribution points added, over 600 van routes closed, reducing fixed S&D cost.
Direct distribution index is about 50-60 versus larger peers; management targets ~75% (sweet spot 75-80%).
Direct distribution is estimated to contribute 2-3 percentage points of volume growth.
A Guwahati factory was outsourced to a third-party-run facility at the start of FY27, which affects comparability of stock-in-trade and inventory figures.
demand_pricing: Almond Drops unit volume growth was double-digit; management says it does not give free volume credit and reports unit volume to exclude extra pack volume.
General trade and organized trade both grew in the mid-20s; rural grew marginally ahead of urban in GT; quick commerce is the fastest-growing sub-channel.
Management said consumer demand has remained resilient so far but it is 'early'; rural and El Nino risks expected to show only when harvest begins.
Management said the category has 91%+ penetration and changing preferences affect only about 1-1.5% of households.
Competitive dynamics: management said peers in other categories have also taken price increases; pricing decisions are set to cover absolute cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is mid-teens growth achievable in FY27 and near double-digit in FY28, given the high base and commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aspiration is double-digit long-term growth and it expects high-teens growth for the year; no guidance beyond that was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ADHO growth comes from distribution, channel, launches or premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot split category versus company action; distribution expansion adds about 2-3 percentage points of volume growth. Price-point packs are in the teens % of value and organized trade is close to 30% of company value.

qa_highlights.question: How should gross margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot predict gross margins given volatile input costs, and is buying only small quantities as it believes costs are at a peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce is a demand-fulfilment channel for large brands like Almond Drops, and a demand-creation plus fulfilment channel for premium and urban products such as serums; strategy is set by brand and market.

qa_highlights.question: Why has stock-in-trade purchase risen relative to materials consumed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to outsourcing production of a Guwahati factory to a third-party-run facility at the start of FY27; detailed queries were directed to the Head of Finance.

qa_highlights.question: How much reported volume growth is due to pack-size (ml-age) reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit volume growth excludes free volume, so ml reductions do not inflate the reported unit volume metric.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from edible oil and West Asia-driven raw material inflation; Q2 gross margin fell sequentially to 59.9%.
Consumer response to the Q3 ~5% price and ml-age increase, and whether unit volume growth holds, especially in rural areas.
Sustainability of ADHO volume momentum and the effect of the brand reinvigoration campaign and higher digital A&P.
Bangladesh operating environment remains tough (grew in the teens).
Management did not provide quarterly guidance, and no gross margin outlook was provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and Almond Drops, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and demand, repeatedly saying outcomes are hard to predict. Management was evasive on the gross margin trajectory, the Q3 price response and split of ADHO growth drivers.
key_quotes: Our endeavor always has been to pass the minimum level of price increase we can to the market, but we also have to be fair to our P&L
In an inflationary environment, our attempt is to protect and grow the absolute EBITDA pool rather than a percentage EBITDA pool.
Has to, Tejas. Otherwise, there's no merit. Now, the delta can be smaller or larger, but it has to eventually show up in growth.

adds.what: Aarohan 2.0 pan-India direct distribution expansion (10% YoY outlet/direct distribution growth; urban reach up 10%, rural higher)

growth.why: Management reiterated high-teens FY27 revenue growth, backed by ~5% Q3 price increase, double-digit ADHO unit volume growth and Aarohan direct distribution expansion (~2-3 pts volume contribution), but gave no specific capacity or order numbers and H1 growth was flattered by a weak base while Q2 revenue rose only 2.7%.
